figures.caption: Native PAGE with 15% acrylamide in 1x TBE. A 10 uM DNA sample was mixed with 6x loading dye and run at 120 V for 40 minutes. The gel was imaged after SYBR Safe staining;  faint green fluorescence was visible, but lane separation and band resolution were limited.
lanes: Lane 1: TMSDY + TMSDS with TMSDX, incubated 10 minutes.
Lane 2: TMSDY + TMSDS with TMSDX, incubated 5 minutes.
Lane 3: TMSDY + TMSDS with TMSDX, incubated 0 minutes.
Lane 4: TMSDY + TMSDS only.
figures.analysis: About four fluorescent bands were observed. Lanes 1-3 migrated similar distances, while lane 4 migrated farther. This pattern was interpreted as consistent with TMSDX displacing TMSDS and binding TMSDY, though the low resolution limited detailed comparison.

figures.analysis: The report suggests the high ion concentration of PBS may have contributed to high current and less distinct bands. The TMSDX and TMSDY controls were again not visible; the TMSDS control in lane 9 was visible.

figures.title: Validation of Aptamer-MB Conjugate Binding to Amyloid Beta-42 (Aβ42) Using Native PAGE
figures.imageAlt: Aptamer gel electrophoresis result with lanes numbered 1 through 10 from left to right.
figures.caption: 20% native PAGE in 1x TBE with SYBR Safe. Aptamer samples at 10 uM were incubated with hemoglobin or amyloid-beta 42 protein, mixed with 2x native sample buffer, and run at 100 V for 60 minutes using the Bento Lab system. Strong fluorescent bands were observed in lanes 5 and 7, with faint bands in lanes 3, 4, and 6.
lanes: Lane 1: empty.
Lane 2: DNA ladder.
Lane 3: aptamer-MB + Aβ42.
Lane 4: aptamer-MB + hemoglobin (specificity control).
Lane 5: non-specific aptamer + Aβ42 (negative control).
Lane 6: aptamer-MB only.
Lane 7: non-specific aptamer only.
Lane 8: Aβ42 only.
Lane 9: hemoglobin only.
Lane 10: empty.
figures.analysis: The fluorescent signals in lanes 5 and 7 correspond to the non-specific aptamer + Aβ42 mixture and the non-specific aptamer-only control. Because SYBR Safe predominantly stains nucleic acids, the protein-only controls in lanes 8 and 9 were not expected to produce strong fluorescence. The fluorescence in the non-specific aptamer samples does not establish specific binding to Aβ42. A distinct mobility shift in lane 3 relative to lane 6, with lane 4 as the hemoglobin specificity control, would support complex formation; no clear shift could be established from the observed fluorescence patterns.

figures.title: Validation of Aptamer-MB Conjugate Binding to Amyloid Beta-42 (Aβ42) Using Native PAGE
figures.imageAlt: Aptamer gel electrophoresis result with lanes numbered 1 through 8 from left to right.
figures.caption: 20% native PAGE in 1x TBE with SYBR Safe. Aptamer samples at 10 uM were incubated with hemoglobin or amyloid-beta 42 protein, mixed with 2x native sample buffer, and run at 100 V for 60 minutes using the Bento Lab system. Strong fluorescent bands were observed in lanes 3, 5, and 8.
lanes: Lane 1: diluted non-target protein (control; 20 uL).
Lane 2: diluted Aβ42 (control; 20 uL).
Lane 3: diluted non-specific aptamer (control; 20 uL).
Lane 4: diluted aptamer-MB conjugate (control; 20 uL).
Lane 5: non-specific aptamer + Aβ42 (negative control; 20 uL).
Lane 6: aptamer-MB + non-target protein (specificity control; 20 uL).
Lane 7: aptamer-MB + Aβ42 (target-binding sample; 20 uL).
Lane 8: DNA ladder (4 uL, approximately 1 ug).
figures.analysis: Lane numbers in the image run from left to right and reverse the loading order recorded in the procedure. The strong fluorescent bands in lanes 3 and 5 correspond to the non-specific aptamer control and the non-specific aptamer + Aβ42 sample; lane 8 is the DNA ladder. Since SYBR Safe predominantly stains nucleic acids, the protein-only controls in lanes 1 and 2 are not expected to produce strong DNA-fluorescence signals. These observations do not establish specific aptamer-Aβ42 binding. A distinct mobility shift in lane 7 relative to the aptamer-MB-only control in lane 4, with lane 6 as the non-target-protein comparison, would be needed to support complex formation; no such shift is established by the documented observations.

figures.title: Methylene Blue Functionality Test With Aptamer
figures.caption: Redox cycling of methylene blue, measured by the time required for the blue oxidized solution to become colourless in the reduced state following exposure to oxygen through shaking.
figures.analysis: Both free methylene blue and the aptamer-MB conjugate retained redox activity, as indicated by reversible colour changes between blue (oxidized) and colourless (reduced) states. Upon shaking, exposure to oxygen caused the solution to become blue, followed by gradual fading to colourless while resting. These observations qualitatively demonstrate that covalent conjugation to the aptamer does not prevent methylene blue from undergoing redox cycling, supporting its suitability as a redox reporter for the biosensor. The 12 trials showed decolourization times ranging from 30 seconds to 4 minutes 14 seconds, indicating variability in the observed reduction times.
